headline: Undeterred by Robertson whiff, Kraken are big-game hunting in trade market
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Kraken are still shopping big after missing on Robertson, with a scoring winger or a top-four defenseman on the list.

Here's why that makes sense even at 9-5-1. Seattle has taken 45.4% of the expected goals (the quality of chances both ways), so it has been outchanced most nights. The record leans on finishing: 52 goals on 42.1 expected, a 9.9-goal cushion that rarely survives a full season. The goalies aren't the reason they're winning either; they've allowed 2.36 more goals than the shots deserved.

So the shopping list fits. A winger who creates chances and a defenseman who limits them both attack the actual gap. Standing pat and hoping the shooting holds is the riskier path for this front office.
